userStories.title: Isolate comparison worktrees and ownership-aware cleanup
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Protect an entire comparison invocation and its individual worktree allocations from competing creation and stale cleanup while deriving tuple-distinct bounded IDs.

**Motivation** — At `5a112f0a2`, the revised review reproduced loss of work in a disposable Git repository (#4), showed that independent package stories can continue after a root `PAUSE` (#1), selected a newer run's log for an older ID and the wrong latest replay across workdirs (#2), and obtained a green CI verdict for expected B despite two head reads reporting A (#3). The worktree regression must protect identical concurrent comparisons, not just ambiguous tuple encodings.

**Approach** — **Compare ownership (#4).** Baseline: `runBakeoff` reclaims stale branches before validation; `WorktreeManager.create` tries to clear the derived path, and `runContestant` cleans up in `finally` even when create failed. Target: acquire exclusive comparison ownership for the checkout before reclaim/create and hold it through cleanup. A contender fails before mutating Git state. Ownership is per invocation, not merely a feature name or a branch prefix. A successful creator may clean its own allocation; a failed or stale owner may not clean a successor's. An existing registered tree with no proof of ownership, including a legacy name, is left intact. Keep branch-only orphan recovery distinct from live-tree replacement. Use the existing checkout lock contract where possible; inner runs must still operate in their own contestant workdirs without deadlocking on the parent lock. Disambiguate the original tuple before lossy sanitization/truncation in both ID namespaces; retain the existing validator, namespace prefixes and 64-character bound.

**Scope** — In: comparison-wide locking on the run --compare CLI path, invocation/allocation ownership, safe create/remove/preflight behavior, typed tuple IDs, affected caller wiring, and unit/integration regressions in packages/nax. Out: operator pause/status propagation (US-002), run/log/replay identity (US-003), and GitHub CI SHA binding (US-004). No automatic deletion or migration of old live worktrees or operator recovery of work already lost. Do not change global stale-lock timeouts or recovery policy.

**Interface** — The spec supplies no new TypeScript signature. Retain the WorktreeId brand and existing producer names `deriveStoryWorktreeId`, `deriveBakeoffWorktreeId`, `storyWorktreePath` and `storyBranchName`; thread verifiable allocation ownership through the manager/contestant cleanup seam rather than equating an ID with an ownership proof.

**Regression design** — Protect the whole comparison, not just a single contestant. Use disposable repositories with a committed feature PRD and valid offline contestant profiles. Hold the winning allocation at a barrier after committing a unique change on its branch and recording that tip and writing a dirty sentinel, then attempt the competing create; do not synchronize with sleeps. For reuse, hold the earlier cleanup callback, retire its allocation, create a successor and only then release the old callback. Update all existing tests listed for US-001 in the shared analysis, preserving verified branch-only/prunable orphan recovery and replacing destructive live-tree replacement expectations. Include a literally seeded legacy `nax/bakeoff-f-agent` tree even after changing derived IDs.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] Within each of deriveStoryWorktreeId and deriveBakeoffWorktreeId, (billing-api, retry-1) and (billing, api-retry-1) yield distinct IDs accepted by validateStoryId. Repeat with (f, a!) versus (f, a?), whose raw inputs differ before sanitization.
[integration] While one run --compare owns the checkout, an identical competing invocation reports a lock conflict before its stale-branch sweep or any contestant create.
[integration] Given two competing WorktreeManager.create requests for the same ID, the losing request leaves the winner's uncommitted sentinel contents intact in its worktree.
[integration] A refused WorktreeManager.create leaves the winner's unique commit reachable by its original branch at the same SHA.

[integration] When create refuses an occupied path, runContestant makes zero calls to the manager's remove method. Include refusal against a seeded legacy tree; changing the derived ID must not let an unconditional cleanup pass just because it targets a different path.
[integration] A delayed runContestant cleanup for an earlier contestant cannot remove the tree of a subsequent owner using the same ID.
[integration] A successful run --compare cleans up its own contestant worktree.
[integration] After a contestant failure a later run --compare can acquire the released outer lock.

[integration] With a live legacy nax/bakeoff-f-agent tree for feature f and profile agent, run --compare leaves its dirty sentinel and original branch tip untouched through preflight and contestant cleanup. Seed the old name literally, not via the changed encoder.

routing.reasoning: Existing checkout-lock, coordinator and manager seams support in-place changes, but comparison-wide exclusion and allocation-generation cleanup span multiple modules and require isolated, barrier-driven regressions against data loss.

modifiedFiles.reason: replace second-create success for a registered live tree with refusal preserving sentinel and branch tip; keep successful recovery of a prunable record whose directory is gone.
calculate expected path and branch using the new bounded tuple ID; preserve isolation and orphan-branch recovery assertions.
preserve refs/nax/orphan namespace but derive the suffix from the supplied typed ID rather than the old encoder spelling.
assert cleanup uses the derived worktree ID rather than the raw story ID; update outdated expected short-name literals.

replace the live-tree force-removal/orphan-ref assertion with refusal and preservation of the live tree; replace the no-tree fixture’s expected removal warning with no attempt to remove an unowned tree. Retain verified branch-only orphan cases.

replace fixed ID, path and branch literal expectations where derived names change with bounded, deterministic, tuple-distinct IDs. Preserve namespace, length and validation assertions, including overlong inputs.
short derived IDs need not equal `bakeoff-f-agent`; retain deterministic, branded and prefix guarantees.
cleanup expectations must distinguish successful allocation from a create failure that confers no ownership.
isolate outer-lock acquisition on the fictitious shared project root; retain the coordinator sequencing and result assertions.
give tests reaching the real coordinator an isolated writable checkout or lock double; keep the PRD and dispatch guards.

userStories.title: Honor operator PAUSE at every between-story boundary
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Consume the root operator queue and stop the run after the current story, persisting run.status=paused without blocking untouched stories or invoking feature finalization.

**Motivation** — At `5a112f0a2`, the revised review reproduced loss of work in a disposable Git repository (#4), showed that independent package stories can continue after a root `PAUSE` (#1), selected a newer run's log for an older ID and the wrong latest replay across workdirs (#2), and obtained a green CI verdict for expected B despite two head reads reporting A (#3).

**Approach** — **Between-story stop (#1).** Baseline: `queueCheckStage` consumes under the selected story's `workdir`, and a pause result marks that story paused. Target: consume operator commands at their run root and distinguish *operator paused run* from *one story needs a human*. The former terminates dispatch without skipping or failing pending work. Extend the persisted run-status union with `paused` for this stop: both project and feature snapshots carry it under `run.status`, not in a story status field. Preserve the current command parser, ordering and dropped-command audit. Package-relative payloads retain their documented resolution semantics. No interruption of an in-flight implementer.

**Scope** — In: root queue consumption, a typed operator-run pause discriminator through stage/pipeline/iteration/dispatch, boundary consumption after an in-flight story including the final one, run-status persistence through completion reconciliation, suppression of runWorkflowFeature until explicit resume, and package-relative INJECT behavior. Out: comparison/worktree ownership (US-001), log identity/replay (US-003), and GitHub head binding (US-004). No mid-story cancellation, queue syntax redesign, or automatic resumption of genuinely blocked stories.

**Interface** — The spec supplies no new TypeScript signature. Extend the persisted run-status union with `paused` and propagate a run-level discriminator independently of ordinary story `pause`; preserve `projectDir` as the run queue root and `workdir` as the selected package payload-resolution base.

**Regression design** — Drive the actual dispatch loop with independent stories and a fake implementer; asserting the first stage's return alone cannot establish the run stopped. Queue root PAUSE while the implementer is held and let that implementer return success. Check both physical status.json files after completion and finish-status reconciliation. Test the final-story boundary before all-passed shortcuts: the story stays passed, the run stays paused, and feature workflow remains held; explicit resume invokes runWorkflowFeature exactly once without rerunning passed work. Retain a control for genuine non-operator story-level pause selecting another independent story and a control for ABORT skipping pending work. INJECT relative.json must read the valid uniquely identified story stored only in the selected package. Update test/unit/pipeline/stages/queue-check.test.ts while retaining queue-consumption and dropped-command auditing assertions.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] When an operator writes PAUSE at the run root during a package story and the fake implementer returns success, the in-flight story finishes with status=passed rather than being interrupted by that PAUSE.
[integration] With two independent package stories remaining, a root PAUSE causes zero further implementer calls in that invocation.
[integration] After completion and finish-status reconciliation return from an operator PAUSE, read both the project and feature status.json files: each has run.status equal to paused.
[integration] Given pending independent stories left untouched by operator PAUSE, their persisted PRD status remains pending, preserving eligibility for selection by a later resumed run.
[integration] Once the root PAUSE has taken effect, the consumed command does not pause the subsequent resume again.
[integration] A non-operator story-level pause result still allows selection of another independent story.
[integration] When the root queue consumes ABORT, pending stories persist as status=skipped, retaining its existing skip-pending behavior rather than adopting pause/resume semantics.
[integration] Operator PAUSE returns from completion without calling the feature-workflow entry runWorkflowFeature (which owns finalization and publication).
[integration] An INJECT relative.json in the root queue adds the valid, uniquely identified story stored only in the selected package’s relative.json to the PRD.
[integration] In a one-story run, queue root PAUSE before the fake implementer returns success: the final PRD retains the story as passed.
[integration] At that final-story boundary, the persisted run.status is paused in both status files even though no stories remain to dispatch.
[integration] At that boundary, runWorkflowFeature is not invoked before explicit resume.
[integration] Resuming the held, all-passed PRD invokes runWorkflowFeature once without rerunning the passed story.

routing.reasoning: The stop discriminator crosses pipeline results, dispatch, completion and two persisted snapshots; final-story/resume boundaries require end-to-end execution regressions rather than a stage-only fix. No authentication or permission changes.

modifiedFiles.reason: the operator PAUSE result may carry a run-level discriminator; continue to verify queue consumption and dropped-command auditing.

userStories.title: Bind run registration, logs and replay to a safe canonical identity
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Give ordinary runs one canonical identity and exact registered log, with safe unavailable behavior and chronological selection across workdirs and filename formats.

**Motivation** — At `5a112f0a2`, the revised review reproduced loss of work in a disposable Git repository (#4), showed that independent package stories can continue after a root `PAUSE` (#1), selected a newer run's log for an older ID and the wrong latest replay across workdirs (#2), and obtained a green CI verdict for expected B despite two head reads reporting A (#3).

**Approach** — **Run artifacts (#2).** Baseline: the CLI opens a timestamped log before invoking the runner, registry metadata records `eventsDir`, exact lookup can fall back to a sibling, and `discoverRun` compares ID strings for latest. Target: use `buildRunId` with the ordinary run workdir, as resume does, before opening a new ordinary run log; persist its actual filename as an optional basename in run metadata relative to `eventsDir` (example: `"logFileName": "run-abcd1234-2026-11-28T10-00-00.000.jsonl"`). Use that filename for the selected record; absent on a legacy record, try only `<runId>.jsonl`. A missing log may degrade replay to metrics/status, never another run's events. Default replay orders by start chronology, not by when the subscriber managed to write the file: source new `registeredAt` values from the runner start instant already on the executor context. Rank valid instants descending, then missing/unparseable instants; within an equal rank and time (including two undated records), retain the descending run-ID tie break. For feature-directory logs, preserve chronological default selection and list ordering for timestamp-only and new canonical filenames. Preserve log rendering apart from extracting the timestamp for the existing list column; registry metadata gains the optional field above. Apply the same filename safety rules to a declared basename and to the legacy exact-name candidate. For an invalid filename report unavailable; never use the mutable latest alias or follow a symlink outside the events directory.

**Scope** — In: canonical ordinary-run ID creation before logger opening and threading into the runner; optional actual log basename and start-time metadata; safe selected-record resolution in logs and replay; chronology/ties in replay discovery and mixed feature-directory filenames; timestamp-only list display; legacy exact-name and resume compatibility. Out: comparison/worktree ownership (US-001), operator pause/status propagation (US-002), and GitHub head binding (US-004). No rewrite of historical JSONL files, registry migration, or guessing legacy log identity from a timestamp, directory order or file modification time. US-003 only: No new CLI switches or changes to log output streams, exit codes or formats apart from the specified selection, timestamp display and unavailable-log behavior.

**Interface** — The spec declares an optional `logFileName` metadata basename relative to `eventsDir`, illustrated above, and retains `buildRunId` as the run-ID producer; it supplies no new TypeScript function signature. Use the runner's existing caller-supplied runId path and thread ctx.logFilePath and ctx.startTime to the real registry subscriber. A present invalid/absent declared log never falls back to a readable exact-ID decoy; only a record without the optional field may try its safe exact legacy filename.

**Regression design** — Exercise real temporary logs and registry records. For replay seed matching per-run metrics with the tested story ID and a JSONL record for that ID at stage `story-orchestrator` with message `Phase passed: older` (distinct phase names in decoys). For filename chronology, use a temporary single-feature project and place the shared runs directory where plain `logs` reads it, under that project’s `.nax/features/<feature>/runs`. Generate IDs for two distinct workdirs with `buildRunId`, assigning the earlier instant to the higher hash. Also exercise a mix with a newer legacy timestamp-only filename in that directory; this tests directory browsing, not guessing an exact registry match. Advance the clock between logger setup and runner start and delay real registry delivery separately, proving ID uses the logger-setup instant while registeredAt uses ctx.startTime. Test both readers against invalid basenames, latest.jsonl, missing declared and legacy candidates, exact-ID decoys, and escaping symlinks, including a legacy exact-name symlink. Preserve rendered log records, output streams/exit codes and normal resume resolution. Replace test/unit/replay/discovery.test.ts's lexicographic latest-ID expectation with valid date ordering and deterministic ties.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] For an ordinary nax run, advance the clock between logger setup and runner start. The log filename stem and its run.start data.runId each equal buildRunId for the resolved workdir and logger-setup instant, including milliseconds.

[integration] Start executeUnified with ctx.logFilePath set to a full path inside the feature runs directory whose basename differs from <runId>.jsonl; after the real registry subscriber drains, meta.json contains only that basename in logFileName.
[integration] With two runs of one feature and an exact-ID decoy for the older one, logs --run <older-id> renders only the older run's sentinel from its declared file.
[integration] With those competing logs, replay <older-id> reconstructs only the older run's declared-file phase.
[integration] When the registered file is absent but a sibling log exists, logs --run <id> reports the requested log unavailable rather than rendering that sibling.
[integration] A legacy registry record without logFileName still resolves an existing exact <runId>.jsonl in both log and replay readers.
[integration] With a legacy exact-name miss, replay <id> reconstructs no phases from a different file in eventsDir.
[integration] With no query, discoverRun returns a DiscoveredRun whose meta identifies the record with the greater valid registeredAt even if that record's workdir hash sorts lower.
[integration] For tied registeredAt instants (or both undated), discoverRun returns a DiscoveredRun whose meta.runId equals the greater run ID.

[integration] Given a dated record and an undated legacy entry (missing or unparseable registeredAt), discoverRun with no query returns a DiscoveredRun whose meta identifies the dated record rather than letting the undated entry outrank it.
[integration] nax resume continues to produce a log resolvable by its registered ID.
[integration] Both readers report unavailable log data for a logFileName that is not a single JSONL basename, even with a readable exact-ID decoy.
[integration] If registration is delayed, executeUnified persists registeredAt equal to the ISO instant of ctx.startTime, not the later wall clock at subscriber delivery.
[integration] A logFileName of latest.jsonl yields unavailable log data in both readers rather than following the mutable alias.
[integration] An escaping symlink under eventsDir yields unavailable log data for both readers, including for a legacy exact-name candidate.
[integration] In the shared feature-directory chronology fixtures, plain logs renders the newest run by the timestamp in its filename, not the greatest filename.
[integration] In the same fixtures logs --list lists the newest run first.
[integration] For hash-prefixed files logs --list renders just the timestamp portion of the stem in the Timestamp column.

routing.reasoning: Existing CLI, subscriber and reader seams support an in-place multi-module fix rather than a new architecture; strict TDD isolation protects filesystem read-access confinement for registered filenames and symlinks as well as legacy identity compatibility.

modifiedFiles.reason: replace the lexicographically greatest-ID latest-run contract with timestamp ordering and deterministic ties.

userStories.title: Bind SHA-less green GitHub wait polls to their recovered stable head
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Reject green expected-head GitHub waits for a known wrong recovered head without changing one-shot, other forge or unknown-head behavior.

**Motivation** — At `5a112f0a2`, the revised review reproduced loss of work in a disposable Git repository (#4), showed that independent package stories can continue after a root `PAUSE` (#1), selected a newer run's log for an older ID and the wrong latest replay across workdirs (#2), and obtained a green CI verdict for expected B despite two head reads reporting A (#3).

**Approach** — **GitHub wait (#3).** Baseline: the stable head recovered by the reads bracketing `gh pr checks` is attached to failed polls but not passing ones. Target on the expected-head GitHub wait only: give an otherwise SHA-less passing poll that same head before expected-head comparison. Do not replace an inline SHA, interpret movement as stability, or change the existing policy when *no* head is available. Keep one-shot, GitLab and commit-check paths unchanged.

**Scope** — In: green fallback-head binding only on expected-head GitHub wait polls and offline public-API unit/integration regressions, retaining mismatch/movement verdicts and the existing unreadable-head policy. Out: comparison/worktree ownership (US-001), operator pause/status propagation (US-002), and run/log/replay identity (US-003). No change to CI readiness policy for a genuinely unreadable head, forge support, poll timing or retry limits. US-004 only: No change to the GitLab, commit-check or one-shot CI paths.

**Interface** — The spec supplies no new TypeScript signature; retain public `waitForChecks` and `readChecksOnce` contracts. The shared bracket helper must distinguish the wait-only green enrichment from its one-shot use, so `readChecksOnce` can retain its final head lookup when its green poll has no inline SHA.

**Regression design** — Exercise the public wait with a scripted forge and bounded clock; do not test only the bracket helper. Extend test/unit/workflow/ci-wait-sha.test.ts to independently script before/after head-only reads, checks and missing or rejected mergeability reads. A/A without inline SHA must not satisfy expected B; B/B must return green for B. Preserve an existing different inline SHA, reject A/B movement on that poll, and retain fail-open behavior when no SHA or one unreadable endpoint prevents a stable bracket. Critically, the one-shot A/A bracket with final lookup B remains green for expected B; adding fallback SHA indiscriminately in the shared helper would skip that final lookup and violate this contract. Keep the existing GitLab, commit-check, retry and timing controls unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] With expected B, stable bracket reads A/A, passing checks and missing inline headRefOid, waitForChecks returns unavailable with head-mismatch detail at deadline.

[unit] With expected B, the same stable bracket reads A/A and passing checks without inline headRefOid, and a rejected mergeability lookup, waitForChecks returns unavailable with head-mismatch detail at deadline rather than green for B.
[integration] With stable B/B and no inline SHA, a passing waitForChecks returns green for expected B.

[unit] When otherwise passing polls already carry an inline SHA different from the expected SHA throughout the bounded wait, waitForChecks returns unavailable at deadline rather than green for the expected SHA.

[unit] Given a checks poll bracket that observes A then B and a bounded clock that reaches the deadline after that poll, waitForChecks returns unavailable with head-movement detail for either expectedSha=A or expectedSha=B, never a green verdict for either observed head on that poll.
[unit] A passing poll with neither inline nor readable fallback SHA returns green from waitForChecks under the existing unknown-head policy.
[unit] With expected B, bracket A/A, no inline SHA and final one-shot lookup B, readChecksOnce retains its green verdict based on the final lookup.
[unit] With one unreadable bracket endpoint and no inline SHA, waitForChecks returns green for passing checks, retaining the existing unknown-head outcome.

routing.reasoning: A narrowly scoped conditional enrichment in the existing poll/bracket path with a wait-only discriminator; bounded-clock public-API regressions protect the shared one-shot helper and unchanged unknown-head/forge policies. No authentication or access-control changes.

analysis:
Existing-system enhancement confined to packages/nax. Implement precisely the four Fix first findings in docs/reviews/nax-v0.94.2-verified-code-review.md:7,19,31,39; findings 5–14 are deferred. Codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this session, so navigation used direct file reads and repository text searches. No implementation code was changed during PRD preparation. The four binding stories have no dependencies or cross-story seams; numbering is a suggested execution order, not a dependency graph. Each must wire its own complete production path and regression.

Architecture and conventions: packages/nax is strict TypeScript/ESM on Bun, with bun:test and injectable _deps seams. Read docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:9–45 before implementation, including its links for dependency injection, error handling, async patterns, path security and testing. Keep production changes in existing modules where practical, preserve barrel boundaries and worktree identity SSOT, use descriptive NaxError context/cause and deterministic tests, and do not add dependencies or change package versions. Package-local commands are bun run test, bun run check:all and bun run typecheck; targeted tests require an explicit path. Never invoke bare bun test or bun run nax. The nax pipeline runs gates; no live providers or network acceptance tests are needed. Tests should restore injected dependencies and isolate temporary repositories, output directories and registry roots; use promise barriers rather than sleeps for concurrency.

US-001 — comparison ownership, allocation generations and tuple IDs. packages/nax/src/worktree/worktree-id.ts:49 and :61 sanitize and join raw tuple members, retaining unhashed short IDs; only collapse at :82 hashes JSON.stringify([rawA, rawB]) for overlong inputs. Consequently short tuple-boundary ambiguities and short sanitize-equivalent raw values collide. Preserve branded WorktreeId, namespace prefixes, validateStoryId and the 64-character bound, but distinguish the original tuple before lossy encoding for every length in both namespaces. The current bounded raw-tuple digest machinery is reusable; avoid deriving identity from already-sanitized inputs. All callers must continue through storyWorktreePath/storyBranchName and naxOrphanRefName, not recreate spelling locally.

The destructive path is packages/nax/src/worktree/manager.ts:301–363: create captures broad worktree-record evidence, prunes, calls remove unconditionally, and can delete a branch. remove at :440 force-removes the derived directory and then deletes its branch. Existing registered live trees are not disposable orphan evidence. Refuse occupied/unowned live allocations without deleting sentinels or moving branch refs, including legacy names. Keep recovery for prunable records whose directories are gone and verified branch-only orphan refs, including the existing exact orphan-tip comparison and conditional ref deletion. Do not make a legacy live tree eligible for sweeping merely because new IDs differ. preserveWorktreeEnv at :74 also invokes cleanup on post-create failure: cleanup there must retain the same ownership guarantee.

packages/nax/src/bakeoff/coordinator.ts:71–83 invokes reclaimStaleBakeoffBranches before validation and has no outer checkout lock; preflight.ts:209 owns the branch-only sweep, and its worktree-list failure guard at :223–227 must continue to fail safely. Acquire comparison ownership before that sweep or create, hold it through all contestant cleanup and release in finally, including failures. packages/nax/src/execution/lock.ts:308 and :401 expose acquireLock/releaseLock with checkout-local nax.lock, atomic publication, stale-record handling and same-process mutation serialization; release currently unlinks by path (:405–422), so reusing the checkout contract does not by itself confer generation-aware contestant cleanup ownership. Use an invocation-specific ownership proof for each successful allocation and check that proof when cleanup executes. A boolean that create once succeeded is insufficient for a delayed callback after allocation reuse. Choose an allocation-handle/token or equivalently guarded cleanup contract without changing global stale-lock timeouts/recovery policy. Preserve checkout-local locking for inner contestant runs: their workdir must remain their isolated tree, not the parent checkout holding the comparison lock.

packages/nax/src/bakeoff/contestant.ts:64–73 types the injected create/remove contract, :153 creates inside try, and :181–186 calls remove unconditionally in finally even when create failed. Adapt the seam and callers so failed create confers no cleanup authority and stale cleanup cannot remove a successor. Preserve dnf-crashed aggregation and sequencing. Manager callers/tests currently expect Promise<void>/undefined, e.g. packages/nax/test/integration/worktree/manager-worktree-id.test.ts:198–199; if introducing a returned allocation proof, update all affected adapters/tests consistently, or retain that API with a separate ownership mechanism. packages/nax/test/integration/bakeoff/coordinator-worktree-isolation.test.ts:50–65 wraps real create/remove and is a useful offline integration seam, but new full comparison fixtures must also commit the feature PRD and provide valid offline profiles rather than bypass every preflight.

Required regression updates for US-001: packages/nax/test/integration/worktree/manager.test.ts:158–163 currently permits a second create; replace that expectation with refusal preserving dirty contents and the original unique branch tip. Retain its prunable-record recovery (:219–228), user-branch protection (:181–198) and verified orphan retry (:509 onward). Update derived path/branch expectations in test/integration/worktree/manager-worktree-id.test.ts and test/unit/worktree/worktree-id.test.ts, including overlong and validation controls. Update test/unit/worktree/nax-orphan-ref.test.ts without changing refs/nax/orphan, test/unit/execution/pipeline-result-handler-worktree-cleanup.test.ts to use the derived typed ID rather than raw story ID/old short literals, and test/unit/worktree/bakeoff-worktree-id.test.ts without requiring the old short spelling. Replace test/unit/worktree/manager.test.ts live-tree force-removal/orphan-ref expectations with preservation, and its no-tree removal-warning fixture with no unowned removal attempt; retain branch-only orphan cases. test/unit/bakeoff/contestant.test.ts must distinguish allocation success from failure. Isolate outer lock acquisition in test/unit/bakeoff/coordinator.test.ts and give test/unit/bakeoff/run-action.test.ts an isolated writable checkout or lock double while retaining PRD/dispatch guards. Run actual concurrent identical comparisons, not just differently encoded tuples. Use a barrier after the winner commits a unique change, records its SHA and writes a dirty sentinel; attempt the competitor while held. For stale cleanup, hold the earlier callback, retire its allocation, create the successor, then release the callback. Migration is deliberately conservative: names change for new allocations only, old live trees remain intact, and no old-tree deletion/migration is introduced.

US-002 — run-level pause through dispatch and completion. packages/nax/bin/run-action-execute.ts:39–46 writes the TUI queue at the run root. packages/nax/src/execution/iteration-runner.ts:132–145 already distinguishes projectDir=ctx.workdir from workdir=resolvedWorkdir for package execution. packages/nax/src/pipeline/stages/queue-check.ts:98–100 consumes from ctx.workdir, which misses that root queue. Read commands at projectDir/run root while preserving ctx.workdir as the base for package-relative INJECT payloads (:172–174); changing both bases would introduce a regression. Preserve processQueueFile atomic consumption, parser/order, and logDroppedCommands (:51–65).

StageAction currently exposes only generic pause at packages/nax/src/pipeline/types.ts:195–205; pipeline/runner.ts:146–147 forwards only finalAction/reason. An explicit operator-run discriminator must survive the stage result, pipeline runner, iteration result and dispatcher rather than infer operator intent from a reason string. packages/nax/src/execution/pipeline-result-handler.ts:324–349 currently marks the selected story paused and persists it for any pause. Retain that behavior for genuine story-level intervention, but operator pause must stop dispatch without changing untouched stories to paused/failed/skipped or overwriting a passed story. ExitReason in executor-types.ts:65 and corresponding results/completion options need a distinct operator stop representation. packages/nax/src/execution/unified-executor-dispatch-phases.ts:193–233 currently continues after an iteration unless stalled/aborted. Propagate the operator stop out of this actual dispatch loop.

A pre-story stage check alone is insufficient. packages/nax/src/execution/unified-executor.ts:209–250 checks PRD completion before dispatch and again when the loop ends. Consume/check the root boundary after an in-flight story settles, including the last allowed iteration and the final story, before any all-passed shortcut or feature workflow. Do not cancel the running implementer. ABORT must retain its pending-to-skipped mutation in queue-check.ts:124–139. Story-level pauses must still allow another independent ready story. Preserve package context for a boundary INJECT even if no next story exists.

Persist paused as run.status in both snapshots: packages/nax/src/execution/status-file.ts:146 owns the current status union and :297 aliases it into RunStateSnapshot; status-writer.ts:140 and :270–276 consume that type. Completion can overwrite earlier status: lifecycle/run-completion-phases.ts:457–477 writes feature status from plugin/cost/completion rules, and :484–511 independently writes project status with completed/stalled/aborted rules. runner-completion.ts:251 onward reconciles final writes again. Carry the operator reason through all these paths so both files remain paused after full completion/finish-status reconciliation even for all-passed PRDs. lifecycle/workflow-run-status.ts:28–33 only downgrades completed to failed; paused must not be coerced into either terminal verdict. end-phase.ts:64–71 currently suppresses feature workflow only for abort, so add an operator-pause guard before calling runWorkflowFeature; that entry owns finalization/publication and must not run on the held invocation. On explicit resume the consumed queue must not reapply pause; existing all-complete execution shortcut at unified-executor.ts:209–212 can reach the workflow once without rerunning passed stories. No automatic resume of genuine human-blocked stories.
